For a super-speciality hospital group whose revenue depends on named clinicians, this constrains both capacity utilisation and the ability to open new units.

risks.note: The sector is described as subject to evolving regulatory requirements and pricing controls on certain medical products and treatments, and changes in the regulatory environment are listed among the Company's business risks. Adverse changes in government policies or reimbursement mechanisms may impact financial and operational performance.

The MD&A names cybersecurity risks associated with digital health systems as an industry threat and cybersecurity and data privacy risks among the Company's own business risks - material given the stated migration of critical applications to the cloud and adoption of electronic health records.

The Company states it faces operational risks relating to patient safety, clinical quality and compliance with applicable healthcare standards. Clinical incidents carry reputational and legal consequences that mitigation relies on internal controls and quality assurance systems to contain.

currentContext.expansion: Expansion during FY2025-26 was almost entirely inorganic and IPO-funded. The Company completed its Initial Public Offering, which closed on December 24, 2025, and its equity shares were listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on December 30, 2025. During the year it acquired stakes in Harmony Medicare Private Limited (100%), Parekhs Hospital Private Limited (100%), Patel Multispeciality Hospital and ICU (51% in a partnership firm) and Patel Pharmacy (51% in a partnership firm), all of which the Board states are operating efficiently; these add hospital and pharmacy footprint at Bharuch, Ahmedabad and Ankleshwar. IPO objects included the proposed acquisition of Parekhs Hospital at Ahmedabad, part-payment of purchase consideration for the already acquired Ashwini Medical Centre, acquisition of additional shareholding in Harmony Medicare Private Limited at Bharuch, funding capital expenditure towards setting up a new hospital in Vadodara, buying robotics equipment for the Gujarat Kidney & Super Speciality hospital at Vadodara, part repayment of secured borrowings, and funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes. Vide a postal ballot proposed by the Board at its meeting held on 19.03.2026 and approved by shareholders on 25.04.2026, two objects were varied without any change in the funds allocated: the new-hospital-in-Vadodara object became healthcare expansion aligned with the Company's main IPO object, including development and operation of a multispecialty hospital project in Bharuch through a newly incorporated private company; and the robotics-equipment object became setting up and operating dialysis services through deployment of dialysis machines and a digital patient monitoring solution by way of collaborating with Lord's Mark Industries Limited. Both varied objects were still substantially unutilised as at 31.03.2026. Post the balance-sheet date, the Company entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Blue Tree Clinics LLC, Dubai, UAE on 08.07.2026 to acquire 51% of its paid up capital. On the technology side, the Company describes itself as a front runner in adopting the latest technology, regularly upgrading infrastructure for scalability and round-the-clock availability and having migrated critical applications to the cloud, and is introducing modern technology and equipment for the treatment of patients across locations. The Audit Committee has periodically reviewed utilisation of the IPO proceeds and management has confirmed the proceeds have been utilised in accordance with the objects of the issue as varied.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Gujarat Kidney and Superspeciality Limited is a Vadodara-headquartered multi-speciality hospital group running facilities across districts of Gujarat and in Dubai, listed on BSE and NSE in December 2025 following its IPO.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: The Company is primarily engaged in the Healthcare Sector, operating multi-speciality hospital infrastructure in districts of Gujarat including Vadodara, Bharuch, Ankleshwar, Godhra, Ahmedabad and Anand, and in Dubai. Medical facilities provided across all locations include Urology, IVF, Gynecology, Orthopedic, Cardiology, Dental and Chiropractic. With an objective of focusing on core business and strategic initiatives, the Company has outsourced its pathological operations and pharmacy management, and has grown through acquisition of hospital and pharmacy entities.

capex_expansion.body: Expansion during FY2025-26 was almost entirely inorganic and IPO-funded. moat.body:

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The MD&A flags a shortage of qualified doctors, nurses and allied healthcare professionals, and lists shortage and retention of skilled healthcare professionals among the Company's business risks. For a super-speciality hospital group whose revenue depends on named clinicians, this constrains both capacity utilisation and the ability to open new units.
- The MD&A cites rising manpower and operating costs and inflationary pressures on medical consumables and equipment, alongside inflationary pressures listed under Risks and concerns. These compress margins where tariff increases lag.
- The sector is described as subject to evolving regulatory requirements and pricing controls on certain medical products and treatments, and changes in the regulatory environment are listed among the Company's business risks. Adverse changes in government policies or reimbursement mechanisms may impact financial and operational performance.
- The MD&A names cybersecurity risks associated with digital health systems as an industry threat and cybersecurity and data privacy risks among the Company's own business risks - material given the stated migration of critical applications to the cloud and adoption of electronic health records.
- The Company states it faces operational risks relating to patient safety, clinical quality and compliance with applicable healthcare standards. Clinical incidents carry reputational and legal consequences that mitigation relies on internal controls and quality assurance systems to contain.
- Increasing competition is the first threat named in the MD&A, together with increasing patient expectations regarding quality of care and service standards - both pressure pricing and require continuing reinvestment in specialty capability.
- The Company lists disruptions arising from public health emergencies or other unforeseen events among its business risks, which can suspend elective procedures and swing occupancy.
- The Company acquired stakes in Harmony Medicare Private Limited, Parekhs Hospital Private Limited, Patel Multispeciality Hospital and ICU and Patel Pharmacy during the year, has signed a Share Purchase Agreement to acquire 51% of Blue Tree Clinics LLC in Dubai, and varied two IPO objects post-listing toward a Bharuch multispecialty hospital and a dialysis-services collaboration - a heavy integration and deployment load, with the varied objects still substantially unutilised as at 31.03.2026.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on the core clinical business by outsourcing pathological operations and pharmacy management

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
